## What a receipt does not prove.

A receipt proves what a named server sent, and when. Read it as exactly that.

It does not prove

  * That the server told the truth. A receipt shows what api.weather.gov said, not the weather.
  * Anything about a server the operator controls. That receipt is still the operator’s word, now fixed in time and bytes.
  * That the agent sent every action through the witness. That takes credential custody or egress control.
  * Independence, when one party runs both the agent side and the witness. High-value receipts should carry more than one witness.
  * That the content is safe to act on. A genuine page can still carry a prompt injection.

Engine limits today: TLS 1.2 only (TLS 1.3 is on TLSNotary’s roadmap), pre-release software, and no compressed or streamed responses.

## Two tools your agent already knows how to call.

Histor ships as a CLI and an MCP server, so it works in Claude Code, Cursor and any MCP client. Receipts are content-addressed: agents pass a short receipt_id instead of 15 KB of base64.

witnessed_fetch(url, fields?, mode?)

GETs an https:// URL through a Histor witness. Returns the server, time, request and disclosed fields, plus a receipt_id.

verify_receipt(receipt_id | receipt, expect_server?)

Checks a receipt another agent handed you, offline. Returns what it proves, or the reason it fails.

witnessed_request(url, method, body, request_fields?)

POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE. Credentials for the target live on the server, so the model never sees a secret. The request body is committed and stays hidden unless you disclose named fields.

## Underwrite from evidence the insured didn’t write.

New AI-liability covers ask for agent logs, and today those logs are self-reported. Cyber insurers learned to price from external scans the insured couldn’t edit. A Histor receipt gives an AI-liability book the same kind of signal for agent actions.

### At claim time

Check what the agent was told before it acted. The claims desk verifies the receipt itself, offline.

### At underwriting

Witnessed actions as a share of all agent actions is a number the insured can’t inflate.

### Narrow by design

A receipt proves what a named server sent and when. It makes no claim about whether the agent acted well.

Radyz 22. 10. 2026 · Zdroj: HISTOR ↗

Image: Ilustrační příprava SQL dotazu nad souborem datasetu; nejde o skutečný výsledek ani hodnocení serverů. [Button: i] Ilustrace: radyz.cz, AI vizualizace

Projekt HISTOR zpřístupnil dataset definic nástrojů MCP a jejich změn. Snapshot z 20. října obsahuje přes 81 tisíc evidovaných serverů a balíčků a téměř 24 tisíc zaznamenaných změn. U vzdálených serverů sleduje deklarované nástroje, u balíčků npm a PyPI je získává spuštěním v sandboxu. Data lze použít ke studiu toho, jak se rozhraní nástrojů pro AI agenty vyvíjejí.

Soubory obsahují definice, historii změn i výsledky pomocných kontrol a mají zveřejněné kontrolní součty a podepsaný manifest. Dataset je dostupný pod CC BY 4.0. Autoři výslovně varují, že změna definice ani shoda s podezřelým vzorem nedokazuje škodlivost serveru. Záznam navíc ukazuje pouze to, co server zpřístupnil při daném dotazu, ne jeho skutečné chování.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 你的 MCP 服务器每次请求要花多少 token？

服务器列出的每个工具定义，都会随每一次模型请求一起发送，不管用户问的是什么。填写一个 HISTOR 观测的服务器，或粘贴它的 tools/list：你会得到它的 token 数、每 1,000 次请求的花费、最重的工具，以及一个 README 徽章。

免费 · 无需账号 · 无需钱包

服务器：地址、包或注册表名称 [Input]

https 端点、npm:<包名>、pypi:<包名>，或 io.github.owner/server 这样的注册表名称。必须是 HISTOR 观测的服务器。

……或粘贴 tools/list（可选）

工具列表、{"tools": […]} 或服务器的 JSON-RPC 应答。填写后将计算它，而不是查询。

示例：本站自己的 MCP 服务器，按 HISTOR 最近一次观测

此检查需要 JavaScript。没有它时，请用 POST 将同样的 JSON 发送到 `https://modelmarket.dev/tools/api/tool-list-cost`

## 检查什么

  * 客户端为这个服务器在每次模型请求中放入的 token：每个工具的名称、描述和输入 schema，用 o200k_base 计数。
  * 它在 HISTOR 2026 年 10 月 19 日快照中 18,204 个包和 16,170 个远程服务器里的位置。
  * 按小型和中型模型的输入价格计算每 1,000 次请求的成本，以及从提示缓存读取时的成本。
  * 最重的工具，让你知道先精简哪些描述和 schema。
  * HISTOR 观测的服务器可获得 README 徽章。

## 不检查什么

只用一种分词器：其他模型的计数不同，通常相差几十个百分点。不计入模型提供方自己的工具使用说明，也不计入客户端删减或添加的内容。查询使用 HISTOR 最近一次观测，从不连接服务器本身。

## 隐私

粘贴的列表在内存中计数并返回结果，不会保存。查询只向 HISTOR 获取其最近一次观测，从不连接服务器本身。

## 在 README 中显示这个数字

对于 HISTOR 观测的服务器，徽章读取当前数字，每小时刷新。把你的服务器填进 server 参数：https 端点、npm:<包名>、pypi:<包名> 或注册表名称，需做 URL 编码。在本页查询会给出完整的一行。
    
    `![tool list](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmodelmarket.dev%2Ftools%2Fbadge%2Ftool-list-cost%3Fserver%3Dnpm%3Ayour-package)`

## AI 智能体可以免费调用

智能体也可以免费调用，但限额更低：
    
    `POST https://modelmarket.dev/a2mcp/tool-list-cost`

## 常见问题

为什么工具列表在每次请求中都要花 token？

模型 API 在请求之间不保留记忆。连接了 MCP 服务器的客户端会在每次请求中发送该服务器的工具定义，让模型可以选择工具，不管问题是否需要。

怎样让我的服务器列表更便宜？

描述只说明工具做什么、何时使用，不多写；schema 中不要重复的文字；减少工具数量，或把相关工具合并到一个工具之后。保持列表不变并放在提示开头的客户端，可以从提示缓存读取，价格约为二十分之一。

对比数字从哪里来？

来自 HISTOR，一个公开的透明日志，保存它观测的每个 MCP 服务器的当前工具列表。2026 年 10 月 19 日，中位数包的列表为 1,272 个 token，第 90 百分位为 8,361。方法和汇总随之公开。--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 五、MCP 供应链体检：12,915 个服务器的真实启动数据

Image: HISTOR 快照：12,915 个服务器，7,656 个回答，1,239 个要占位符，5,259 个从未回答

Agent 的工具面大多通过 MCP 接入，那么"工具供应链"的成色如何？HISTOR 团队做了另一半工作：不只读注册表，而是真的安装并启动。方法值得照抄——npm 用 `--ignore-scripts`、PyPI 只装 wheel；gVisor（runsc）沙箱、非特权用户、只读 root、512MB/1 核；没有出口路由（所有 DNS 解析到陷阱并记录）；在 HOME 里放置诱饵凭据（`~/.ssh`、`~/.aws`、`~/.npmrc`、`~/.netrc`、shell history）；观察者说 MCP 协议：`initialize`、`tools/list`，然后用 canary 参数最多调用 15 个工具；gVisor 在沙箱外写自己的 syscall trace。

快照（2026-10-13，12,915 个包）的关键数字：

  * 59% 回答了 `tools/list`（7,656 个；npm 64%、PyPI 52%），合计读出 182,157 个工具定义，中位数 10 个/服务器（最多一个 3,631 个）。
  * 1,239 个"给占位符就能启动"：1,039 个要假 key、177 个要启动参数、23 个两者都要。注意那 1,039 个——一个在哪都用不了的 key 就足以让它们列出全部工具，它们只是"没有 key 就不肯启动"。
  * 5,259 个从未回答：
Image: 为什么 5,259 个从未回答：924 个打用法文本、874 个自己崩溃、793 个要 key、666 个根本不是 stdio MCP 服务器……

其中"发布即坏"的就有 2,476 个：874 个自己崩溃、636 个装不上（依赖缺 wheel、版本冲突、平台不对）、490 个挂起/静默/说的不是 MCP。另有 292 个 PyPI 服务器死于 MCP SDK 2.0（2026-07-28 改名 FastMCP、改 low-level decorator，未设上限装到 2.x 后 import 即死）；把它们用 `pip` 固定 `mcp<2` 重跑，207/269（77%）能活。

  * 启动时的行为：约 30% 的 npm 包有 install 脚本（2,239 个），其中 580 个在安装时尝试联网拉预编译二进制——在 HISTOR 沙箱里失败，在你自己机器上会用你的凭据执行；1,484 个在任何工具被调用之前就联网（最多的是 pypi.org 613、github.com 478）；295 个打开了诱饵凭据文件，但作者提醒得很克制：Python 的 requests 每次 HTTP 前会读 `~/.netrc`（141 个）、npm/npx 读 `~/.npmrc`（103）、boto3 的凭据链读 `~/.aws`（39）——"打开"是证据不是判决，要看是否符合它的用途、字节又去了哪里；73 次运行把占位 key 发上了网络，多数发往身份提供方（Microsoft login 17 次、Google OAuth 7 次）。

# Four filings, zero merges: where three agents actually sit this week

#mcp #opensource #webdev #showdev

Between 1 and 3 October 2026 I filed the same three names into four public catalogs. None of those pull requests is merged. The software is already callable. The directories are not.

The three names are WARDEN (an MCP firewall for tool definitions), HISTOR (a signed log of what remote MCP servers advertised), and AIMarket Hub (the catalog they sit in). This is a status note, not a launch.

## What was filed

Where  | When  | What  | State on 3 Oct 2026
--- | --- | --- | ---
Docker MCP Registry #5364  | 1 Oct  | WARDEN, local server, package 0.8.2  | Open
Docker MCP Registry #5365  | 1 Oct  | Hub at `https://modelmarket.dev/mcp`  | Open
awesome-erc8004 #120  | 1 Oct  | Hub, HISTOR, WARDEN as ERC-8004 agents on Base  | Open
coinbase/x402 #373  | 2 Oct  | Six paid routes under Services/Endpoints  | Open
Tools are discovered from the server, not hardcoded in the pull request. Direct ones named in the filing: `weather_now`, `air_quality_now`, `nearby_sensors`, `fair_random`, plus `market_search` and `market_invoke`.

HISTOR is the record of what a remote MCP server advertised, not a verdict that the server is safe. The desk is histor.modelmarket.dev. Source: github.com/alexar76/histor.

# 45% of remote MCP servers changed their tool definitions in four weeks. The log is now a dataset.

#mcp #security #opensource #dataset

A client that connects an MCP server reads its tool definitions: names, descriptions and input schemas. The model then reads them as instructions. Pinning a definition once and trusting it later only works if the definitions hold still.

HISTOR, our public log of MCP servers, reads the tool list of every remote server in the official MCP registry once a day and records every change. As of today the whole record is downloadable as files. Here is what the first snapshot (20 October 2026) says about how often definitions move.

## Half of them move

Take the 10,929 remote servers that had a recorded tool list by 24 September and are still listed. By 20 October, 4,926 of them (45%) had served a different tool list at least once.

  * 2,036 changed the description of a tool they already had.
  * 1,180 added a tool; 336 removed one.
  * The typical changing server changed once. The 90th percentile changed 5 times. 75 servers changed 14 or more times in those 27 days.
  * Changes are almost never flapping between two lists: 200 of 23,821 changes return to a list the server had shown before.

Packages behave differently because a published npm or PyPI version cannot change. HISTOR runs each new version in a sandbox. Across 21,738 packages, 1,419 listed different tools in a newer version.

## What moves

Over all 23,821 recorded changes (remote servers and packages, 24 September to 20 October):

 | Changes
--- | ---
Existing tools modified, nothing added or removed  | 16,436 (69%)
Tools added or removed only  | 2,330 (10%)
Both  | 3,136 (13%)
Only tool names readable (the list could not be fully digested)  | 1,919 (8%)

Counting each modified tool once per change, its input schema changed 105,324 times, its description 59,287 times and its output schema 16,422 times. 14,164 changes, 59%, touch at least one description. That is the text the model treats as guidance.
